summary_paragraph: A 54-year-old woman with a history of Crohn’s disease, short bowel syndrome, and multiple prior abdominal surgeries was admitted for acute abdominal pain and projectile vomiting following an abdominal massage. She was recently hospitalized for similar symptoms attributed to pseudoobstruction. On admission, she was in distress with tachycardia and abdominal distension. An NG tube was placed, revealing dilated bowel loops on imaging, but CT scan showed no mechanical obstruction, supporting a diagnosis of pseudoobstruction. She was managed with NPO status, IV fluids, pain control, and serial monitoring. Her renal function improved with hydration, and after two enemas, she passed stool and gradually advanced to a regular diet. The NG tube was repositioned multiple times before being removed. She remained stable, with no medication changes, and was discharged home in good condition able to tolerate oral intake without pain or vomiting.
problems: Dyspepsia and other specified disorders of function of stomach
